The ATT estimate is **0.010** (0.0103, from inverse-propensity weighting of the controls).

I used a logistic-regression propensity score on x0–x16, then compared the outcome mean of the 237 treated units with the propensity-odds-weighted mean of the 2,333 controls. This is the standard textbook ATT estimator, and I chose it as the headline. The estimate depends on the method, though:

| Method | ATT |
|---|---|
| IPW (propensity odds weighting) | 0.0103 |
| Doubly robust (AIPW) | 0.0125 |
| Outcome regression, logit | 0.0144 |
| Outcome regression, OLS | 0.0200 |
| 1-NN matching on propensity score | 0.0338 |
| 1-NN matching on standardized covariates | -0.0084 |

Every method puts the effect near zero, roughly -0.01 to 0.03. The point estimate is sensitive to the estimator, so treat 0.010 as a reasonable central value rather than a precise number. I did not compute standard errors.

ANSWER: 0.010
